text:
morgan: Heads up — seeing ~0.5% of requests attributed to `unknown-claim` after yesterday's SA key rotations in prod. Dashboard spike around 09:12 UTC. https://console.redwood.internal/telemetry/claims?from=1715120000

sam: :eyes: can you paste a query snippet and an example request id?

morgan: request id rq_8b3f2a, logs show `claim_id` null and `key_id` present. Query that found the delta:
```sql
SELECT claim_id, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM request_events WHERE ts > 1715119000 GROUP BY claim_id ORDER BY cnt DESC;
```
results show a small bucket of `NULL` claims but valid key ids.

jin: my guess: claim resolution cache expired at rotation and fallback path drops claim instead of mapping to org/project. We added a soft-fail path in auth-proxy a while back.

tess: agreed. I think two things: (1) add a nightly "claim-sweep" job to reconcile key->claim using recent audit logs, and (2) surface a "probable owner" on the console with confidence score so customers see where billing might land.

eli: UX note: if we show "probable owner", we must annotate how confident it is and offer a one-click request to claim or request support. Otherwise SRE/support will get flooded.

sam: +1 on sweep job. Implementation idea: iterate keys with null claims -> look up last 24h request footprints -> heuristic match to tenant IP/labels -> write reconciliation record to a new telemetry table. Pseudocode:
```py
for key in keys_with_null_claims():
  candidates = find_tenants_by_ip_and_labels(key.last_requests)
  if candidates and score(candidates[0]) > 0.75:
    write_reconciliation(key.id, candidates[0].id, score)
```

morgan: how expensive will that be? we run this across 100s of millions of events. Need to shard and rate-limit.

jin: can be incremental and windowed: only keys active in last 48h. Use pre-aggregated fingerprint table we already populate for routing telemetry. That keeps cost bounded.

tess: I'll prototype the console wireframe showing the "probable owner" flag + explainers. Also will add an opt-in toggle for automatic claim reconciliation for org admins.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of auth-proxy v2.14.1 started at 1715123500 — 3/10 hosts. No errors so far.

eli: side question — how should quotas behave while reconciliation is pending? If a key has null claim but we can guess owner, do we route quota/billing to guessed org or hold?

sam: I vote: don't change quota attribution until manual confirmation or admin opt-in. Auto-attribution is risky. Put guessed attribution into "provisional" state and surface in billing UI with expiry.

jin: provisional attribution + separate metric works for us. We can also emit alerts when provisional share exceeds X% of total for a tenant.

morgan: ok sounds like plan. Next steps: jin to scope sweep job (est cost/ops), tess to mock console changes, sam to add provisional-attribution enum to billing proto, eli to draft support playbook. I'll pair with jin for rollout gating.

tess: I'll post wires in #design once ready.

sam: I'll start a proto CL for the billing enum and feature flag.

morgan: thanks everyone. tagging @here for visibility. :thumbsup:
